identity.title: Optimistic Task Inference for Behavior Foundation Models

problem.claim: Infer and optimize a task at test time through interaction with the environment, without directly specified rewards or extensive reward labeling.

contributions.claim: OpTI-BFM models uncertainty over reward functions and uses an optimistic decision criterion to guide data collection for task inference.
The authors provide a regret bound for well-trained BFMs by connecting the analysis to upper-confidence algorithms for linear bandits.

stated_novelty.claim: The proposed approach performs task inference purely through test-time environment interaction while directly modeling reward-function uncertainty.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that, on established zero-shot benchmarks, OpTI-BFM enables successor-features-based BFMs to identify and optimize an unseen reward function within a handful of episodes, with minimal compute overhead.

narrative_sequence.summary: BFMs can retrieve a high-performing policy for a reward function specified at test time, enabling zero-shot RL.
This process may require computing rewards on a non-negligible inference dataset, assuming a usable reward function or substantial labeling effort.
The paper proposes interaction-only task inference with OpTI-BFM, using optimistic uncertainty-guided collection and a linear-bandit-based regret bound.
The authors report benchmark results showing rapid unseen-reward identification and optimization with minimal compute overhead.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns the proposed decision rule with both an explicit uncertainty model and a formal regret connection, then reports a benchmark outcome under a stated BFM class.

lessons.interpretation: This pairing makes the method's decision principle, theoretical framing, and reported scope easier to relate.
lessons.application: When introducing a task-inference method, state what uncertainty it models, how that uncertainty changes data collection, and which model class and evaluation setting support the claim.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when uncertainty is not central to the method or when the work has no meaningful theoretical or empirical scope conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not quantify “a handful of episodes” or “minimal compute overhead,” nor specify baseline comparisons or benchmark names.
The assumptions and exact conditions behind the regret bound are not given beyond well-trained BFMs and its connection to linear-bandit algorithms.
